transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in to see me?
To be honest, it's a bit hard for me to talk about. Once I start eating late at night after my shift, I feel like I can’t stop or control how much I’m eating.

When these late-night eating episodes happen, do you eat a very large amount of food in a short time and feel out of control, and do you ever try to make up for it by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising?

Yes, I put away a massive amount of food—honestly, enough to feed a family of four—and once I get going, it feels like I'm on autopilot and just can't stop. But I've never tried to throw it up, use laxatives, or starve myself the next day to make up for it.
Have you ever had periods of eating much less than usual, strict dieting, or fasting for weight control, even if you do not vomit or use laxatives?
No, I haven't really ever tried strict dieting or fasting to control my weight. I just try to eat normally during the day, but then the late-night eating still happens.
Do these late-night eating episodes cause you a lot of distress, or do you worry strongly about your weight or body shape because of them?

Yes, it causes me a lot of distress and shame, and afterward I just sit there feeling gross and wondering how a grown man and shift supervisor can lose control like that. I worry constantly about the rapid weight gain too. It makes me feel sluggish, and I'm so embarrassed by it that I've started skipping church potlucks and avoiding people altogether.
Do these episodes mainly happen only at night after your shift, with little or no eating during the day, and do you ever wake up from sleep to eat?

They definitely happen late at night right after my shift, but I don't think I've ever woken up from sleep just to eat. As for the daytime, my schedule is so turned around now that I'm not really sure how much I'm actually eating then.

On most days, do you eat a large portion of your calories after dinner or after your shift, with little appetite or little eating earlier in the day? Also, do you ever wake up from sleep specifically to eat?

I eat those large amounts right after my shift before I go to sleep, rather than waking up in the middle of the night to eat. I'm not really sure about having a lack of appetite earlier in the day, as my main issue is just that uncontrollable eating when I get home from my night shift.
Do these episodes happen at least once a week for the past 3 months, or have they been going on for a different amount of time?

Yes, they've been happening several times a week for at least the last three or four months. The whole pattern really started about five months ago when I took on the night-shift supervisor role and my routine got thrown off.

Before your night-shift episodes started, did you regularly eat most of your food in the evening or at night with very little eating earlier in the day, or did this pattern begin only after the shift change?

Before the promotion, I had a pretty regular, normal meal routine, though I'm not entirely sure about the exact breakdown of how much I ate during the day back then. This out-of-control late-night eating pattern definitely only started after my shift changed.
Before your night-shift schedule started, did you already regularly eat most of your food late in the evening or at night, or did that pattern begin only after the shift change?

No, I never ate like this before the shift change. Prior to taking the supervisor role about five or six months ago, I had very regular routines around my meals, sleep, and church. This late-night eating only started as a way to decompress from the stress of the new job, and it quickly spiraled into a habit.

Do you usually eat most of your daily food intake after your shift or in the evening, with little appetite or little eating earlier in the day? Or are the binge episodes more separate, unpredictable episodes that happen regardless of your normal meal pattern?

It's definitely a regular pattern of eating late at night after my shift to help me decompress from the work stress. As for my daytime eating or if my appetite is lower earlier in the day, I'm not really sure because I haven't paid much attention to that.

Before your shift change, did you usually eat most of your food in the evening or at night with very little eating earlier in the day, or did this late-night eating pattern start only after you began working nights?

No, this late-night eating pattern definitely only started after my shift changed. Before my promotion six months ago, I had regular, long-standing meal routines and didn't eat like this at all. It only began as a way to decompress after my midnight shifts, and it has evolved into this out-of-control pattern over the last five months.

When you eat late at night after your shift, do you usually feel little or no appetite earlier in the day and end up getting most of your daily food after dinner or after work, or are these episodes more like separate binges that happen regardless of your usual eating pattern?

I'm not really sure about my appetite during the day or if I'm eating most of my food then. But I do know that the late-night eating after my shift is when I feel completely out of control and just can't stop.

Do you usually eat most of your daily food after your shift or in the evening with little eating earlier in the day, or are these late-night episodes separate binge episodes that happen even when you have eaten normally during the day?

I haven't paid close attention to how much I eat during the day since my shift work messed up my routine, so I'm not entirely sure about that. But these late-night episodes feel like completely uncontrollable binges once they start, regardless of how I've eaten earlier.

During a typical day, do you usually eat very little until late evening or after your shift and then consume most of your calories at that time, or do these late-night episodes happen as separate binge attacks even when you have eaten normally earlier in the day?

I'm not entirely sure whether I'm eating normally earlier in the day, as my whole meal routine has been completely disrupted since starting the night shift. I just know that once I get home after midnight, I lose all control and eat a massive amount of food.

Do you usually go through most of the day with little or no appetite and then eat most of your food late in the evening or after your shift, or are these mainly separate binge episodes that can happen even after you’ve eaten normally earlier in the day?

Like I mentioned, I'm really not sure about my daytime appetite or if I eat normally then, because my schedule is so turned around. The main thing I know for sure is that when I get home late at night, I have these massive, uncontrollable eating episodes. That's the real problem I can't seem to stop.

When you eat late at night after your shift, is it mainly because you’ve eaten very little earlier in the day and then make up most of your calories at night, or do you have separate binge episodes even when you’ve eaten normally earlier?

I'm not entirely sure and haven't paid close attention to how much I'm eating during the day. The late-night eating feels more like a way to decompress from the stress and feeling wired after my shift, rather than just satisfying normal hunger.

On most days, do you eat very little during the day and then make up most of your calories late at night after your shift, or do you have separate binge episodes that happen even when you’ve eaten normally earlier in the day?

I haven't really paid close attention to how much I eat during the day, so I'm not entirely sure if I'm eating normally then. But the main, out-of-control episodes definitely happen late at night when I get home after my shift.

Before your late-night episodes, do you usually eat very little during the day and then make up most of your calories after your shift, or do these episodes happen even when you’ve eaten normally earlier in the day?

I'm honestly not sure about my daytime eating patterns because the night shift has completely thrown my whole meal schedule out of whack. I can't really say if I'm restricting or eating normally during the day. I just know that once I get home after my shift, that's when things get out of hand.

On most days, do you eat very little during the day and then make up most of your food intake after your shift at night, or do you have separate binge episodes that happen even when you’ve eaten normally earlier in the day?

I'm really not sure about my exact daytime eating patterns or if I'm restricting during the day. I just know that when I get home from my night shift, I feel incredibly hungry and wired, and that's when the out-of-control eating happens.

On most days, do you intentionally or unintentionally eat very little during the day and then make up most of your food intake after your shift at night, or do you have separate binge episodes that happen even when you’ve eaten normally earlier in the day?

I'm not entirely sure and haven't paid close attention to my daytime eating habits since my schedule was disrupted. I just know that I come home after my night shift feeling incredibly hungry, wired, and ready to eat.

Do you usually eat very little during the day and then make up most of your food intake after your shift at night, or do you have separate binge episodes that happen even when you’ve eaten normally earlier in the day?

I'm really not sure and haven't paid much attention to how much I eat during the day since my schedule got so disrupted. I just know that when I walk through the door after my night shift, I'm incredibly hungry, wired, and ready to eat.

When you get home after your shift, do you usually eat most of your daily food intake because you barely ate earlier in the day, or are these separate binge episodes that happen even when you’ve eaten normally during the day?

I honestly haven't tracked my daytime eating closely enough to compare or know for sure. I just know that I definitely come home feeling very hungry and wired after my shift, and once I start eating, I just can't seem to stop.

Before these late-night episodes started, did you usually eat most of your food late in the evening or at night with little appetite earlier in the day, or did this pattern begin only after your night-shift schedule changed?

This pattern definitely only started after my night-shift schedule changed. Before my promotion about six months ago, I had regular, long-standing routines around my meals and sleep, and I didn't eat like this at all. The new night shift disrupted everything and that's when these late-night eating episodes began.

When you come home after your shift, do you usually eat most of your food for the day at that time because you ate very little earlier, or are these true binge episodes that happen even if you’ve eaten normally during the day?

While I do come home feeling wired and hungry after my shift, these are definitely true binge episodes where I completely lose control. Once I start eating, a switch flips and I go on autopilot, consuming massive amounts of food—like enough for a family of four—even when I try to tell myself to stop.

Outside of these late-night episodes, do you usually eat very little during the day and then make up most of your calories after your shift, or do these happen as separate binge episodes even when you’ve eaten normally earlier in the day?

I'm really not sure and haven't paid close attention to my daytime eating habits compared to what happens late at night. I just know that once I get home after midnight, I lose all control and eat a massive amount of food.

Before the late-night episodes, do you usually eat very little during the day and then make up most of your calories after your shift, or do these episodes happen even when you’ve eaten normally earlier in the day?

I'm not entirely sure and haven't paid close attention to my daytime eating habits. But by the time my night shift ends, I just feel incredibly hungry and wired, and that's when I end up losing control.

Before your night shift started, did you usually eat most of your food late in the evening or at night with little appetite earlier in the day, or did this late-night eating pattern begin only after the shift change?

This late-night eating pattern definitely only started after my shift changed. Before my promotion about six months ago, I had regular, long-standing routines around my meals and sleep, and I didn't have any of these late-night eating issues. It was only after the new shift disrupted everything that this started.

Do you feel that you eat most of your daily food intake late at night because you barely eat earlier in the day, or are these separate binge episodes that happen even when you have eaten normally earlier?

I haven't really tracked my daytime eating closely, so I'm not entirely sure about that. I just know that I come home from my shift feeling extremely hungry and wired, and eating has become my main way to decompress from all the work stress.

On most days, do you eat very little during the day and then make up most of your food intake after your shift at night, or are these separate binge episodes that happen even when you’ve eaten normally earlier in the day?

I aren't entirely sure because I haven't paid close attention to how much I eat during the day. I just know that when I get home after my night shift, I feel incredibly hungry, wired, and ready to eat.

Do you usually eat most of your daily food after your shift at night because you eat very little earlier in the day, or are these separate binge episodes that happen even when you’ve eaten normally during the day?

I'm not entirely sure and haven't really thought about how much I eat during the day versus at night. I just know that once I start eating after my shift, it feels like an uncontrollable episode that I can't seem to stop.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has recurrent, clearly binge-like episodes with loss of control, marked distress, shame, and social avoidance, occurring several times per week for 3–4 months. The pattern began only after a night-shift change and is described as late-night eating after work rather than a longstanding pattern of eating most calories in the evening with little intake earlier in the day. There is no compensatory vomiting, laxative use, fasting, or exercise. This is most consistent with other specified feeding or eating disorder rather than unspecified feeding or eating disorder.
